question: Which of the following types of lube oils are used in airline industries?
solution:
The correct answer is __Synthetic lubricants****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Synthetic lubricants__ are widely used in the airline industry.
 
• These lubricants are man-made chemical compounds designed to perform under extreme conditions.
 
• They provide excellent thermal stability, ensuring smooth engine performance at high altitudes.
 
• Synthetic lubricants also offer resistance to oxidation, reducing wear and tear on components.
 
• These oils are preferred in aviation due to their longer service life and enhanced performance.
 
• They help in maintaining reliability and efficiency of aircraft engines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Petroleum Lubricants:**
 
 
• These are derived from crude oil but are less stable under high temperatures and pressures.
 
• Not commonly used in modern aviation due to performance limitations.
 
 
 
• **Grease and Bee Wax Lubricants: **
 
 
• These are used for specific applications but are not suitable for aircraft engines.
 
• Limited to low-speed or low-temperature conditions.
 
 
 
• **Biodiesel Lubricants:**
 
 
• Primarily used in ground vehicles and not suitable for aviation engines.
 
• Lack the necessary performance characteristics for high-altitude conditions.
